jobs.prompt:
Goal g-08a347e1 (owner priority, Opus review before merge), core module only - CLI wiring is a separate follow-up ticket, do not touch tools/inbox-commands.mjs or any other file. tools/backlog.mjs's read-modify-write cycle (readBacklog then writeBacklog) has NO lock and NO version check - two concurrent writers can race and silently wipe each other's change. Read tools/backlog.mjs in full as context first. Read tools/ledger-lease.mjs as context for the EXACT established locking pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase for a similar shared-state file: acquireAutopilotLock(root, { name: 'leases' }) wraps the whole read-modify-write cycle in a try/finally, releasing the lock in finally - reuse this exact pattern with name: 'backlog', do not invent a different locking mechanism. Read tools/autopilot-lock.mjs as context only (do not edit it) to confirm acquireAutopilotLock's real signature.

Implement all of the following in tools/backlog.mjs ONLY:

(1) Wrap every mutating operation - addGoal, removeGoal, markStarted, markDone, and the two NEW operations below - in acquireAutopilotLock(root, { name: 'backlog' }) / try-finally-release, exactly like ledger-lease.mjs's claim/renew/release. readBacklog itself (read-only) does not need the lock.

(2) Add a version field (a monotonic integer counter, starting at 1 on first write) to the stored backlog.json shape. readBacklog's return value should now also include this version (e.g. { items, version }) - update the existing 'a missing backlog reads as empty' test in tests/backlog.test.mjs to expect the new field. Every successful write increments version by exactly 1. Before writing, re-read the on-disk file under the lock and refuse the write (throw backlog-stale-write) if the on-disk version no longer matches the version read at the start of the operation.

(3) Add a guard on the write path: if the new item count is LOWER than the previous count by MORE than 1, and the caller did not explicitly mark this write as an intentional multi-item removal, refuse with backlog-unexpected-drop (the owner's literal ask). removeGoal (removes exactly one item) and the new bulk-replace import operation (see (5)) are the only two paths allowed to reduce the count - removeGoal passes an explicit single-item-removal intent; import passes an explicit bulk-replace intent (uncapped). Every other path (addGoal, markStarted, markDone, move) must never reduce the count.

(4) Add moveGoal(root, id, { to }) where to is 'top', 'bottom', or { after: otherId } - reorders the one item without changing its status or any other field. Refuse (backlog-unknown) if the id, or the after reference id, doesn't exist. Reorder-only: never removes or duplicates an item.

(5) Add exportBacklog(root) (returns { items, version }, read-only, no lock needed) and importBacklog(root, { items }) (validates every incoming item via the existing validateStored, then REPLACES the entire item list under the lock, incrementing version, marked as an intentional bulk-replace for the guard in (3)). Reject malformed input using the existing validation/error codes.

(6) Add a rotating backup: after every successful write, copy the just-written backlog.json into a small rotating history (e.g. .swarm/project/backlog-backups/backlog.<version>.json), pruning so at most the 10 most recent are kept. Best-effort after the real write succeeds; a backup failure must never fail or roll back the real write.

Write tests in tests/backlog.test.mjs (extend, keep existing coverage beyond the one noted shape update): two concurrent addGoal calls never lose an item; a stale on-disk version is refused with backlog-stale-write; an attempted write dropping more than one item outside removeGoal/importBacklog is refused with backlog-unexpected-drop; moveGoal reorders correctly for top/bottom/after ID, never changes item count, refuses an unknown id; exportBacklog/importBacklog round-trip exactly, importBacklog rejects a malformed item; after 11+ writes at most 10 backup files exist, oldest pruned; a backup-write failure does not block the real write. STANDING TEST RULE: every test that spawns a process must set a per-test timeout of 60000 ms or less and kill children in its after hook. Run the test file when done.
